# Dimension: Isolation on k3s and Security Record

Covers the Kubernetes path (NVIDIA OpenShell's Kubernetes driver,
kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox, k3s specifics), each harness's Kubernetes
deployment options, and the 2025–2026 vulnerability record. Sources are in
[citations.md](../citations.md).

## Kubernetes path status (vs the June 2026 finding)

The prior topic
([hermes-agent-k3s-openshell-billing](../../hermes-agent-k3s-openshell-billing/))
found the OpenShell chart experimental and "not for production", and k3s
unnamed by NVIDIA.

| Item | Now (2026-11-05) | Source |
|---|---|---|
| OpenShell Helm chart banner | Still "Experimental - the Kubernetes deployment path is under active development. Expect rough edges and breaking changes." | [28] |
| Same README | Semver tags "Recommended for production" | [28] |
| Support matrix | Kubernetes "Supported through the OpenShell Helm chart" | [26] |
| Release-stability RFC | State "review"; Helm listed as a stable-surface class; Kubernetes driver not named | [30] |
| k3s named by OpenShell? | **No.** The Helm README mentions k3d only for the unsafe `allowUnauthenticatedUsers` flag | [28] |
| OpenShell k8s prerequisites | Kubernetes 1.29+; "CNI that enforces ingress and egress NetworkPolicy"; Agent Sandbox CRDs first | [27] |
| CNI warning | "Without enforcement, sandbox workloads may reach the network directly and bypass supervisor policy." | [27] |
| agent-sandbox version | v1.0.9 latest (2026-10-29). v1.0.0 (2026-08-28) moved APIs to v1beta1, "removing legacy v1alpha1 support" | [36] |
| agent-sandbox project status (Mar 2026) | "currently in development under SIG Apps"; "the project is moving fast" | [37] |
| agent-sandbox tested platforms | KinD and GKE; "tested with the newest Kubernetes release" | [34] |
| agent-sandbox quickstart default | "By default it uses a basic KIND cluster without container isolation"; gVisor/Kata optional | [33][35] |
| k3s network policy | "K3s includes an embedded network policy controller… kube-router's netpol controller library". Egress enforcement not stated | [39] |
| Rootless k3s | "Experimental", cgroup v2 only, single node | [40] |

**Contradictions:**

- NVIDIA's own pages disagree with each other. The chart README is labelled
  "Experimental" [28]. The support matrix lists Kubernetes as "Supported" [26],
  and the same README recommends semver tags for production [28].
- bex.co says v1beta1 arrived "with the v0.5.0 release in June 2026" [38]. The
  release page places it at v1.0.0 in August 2026 [36]; v0.5.0 appears there
  only as an upgrade prerequisite. The higher-tier source [36] is used.

**Open question.** OpenShell needs a CNI that enforces egress NetworkPolicy
[27]. The k3s docs confirm an embedded policy controller but do not state
whether it enforces egress [39]. Only a test on the user's cluster would
answer this.

**Advisory hygiene differs.**
- The Hermes GitHub advisories page reads "There aren't any published security
  advisories" [126]. Meanwhile OpenCVE lists 45 Hermes CVEs [125], and one
  disclosure says the vendor "did not respond in any way" [123].
- opencode lists three published advisories [72]. It patched the MCP OAuth RCE
  "without a CVE or security advisory" and called malicious MCP servers
  "outside their threat model" [73].
- Inference: a missing advisory is not evidence that a project is safe.

**A recurring pattern (inference from [89][122]).** Hermes and Goose both had
RCE from a cloned repository's `.git/config` `core.fsmonitor`. In Goose it ran
"before goose contacts a model and without a submitted prompt, model call, tool
approval, or trust prompt" [89]. In Hermes it ran when the user "sends any
message" [122]. Agent-level approvals do not cover the harness's own git calls,
so only an outer sandbox contains this class.

### Harnesses used as attack tools

- **Carbonato.** Attackers compromised Docker daemons exposed without
  authentication on port 2375, launched a privileged container with `/:/host`,
  and installed unmodified Hermes driven over Telegram [127][128]. The IOC
  environment variable `GATEWAY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS` [128] is the setting Hermes'
  checklist says never to use [12].
- **Nx npm compromise (Aug 2025).** Malicious Nx releases invoked the `claude`,
  `gemini` and `q` CLIs for reconnaissance and theft [129].
- **Goose red team.** Block's own team "compromised a Block employee's laptop
  using a prompt injection attack hidden in invisible Unicode characters" [90].

## Counter-evidence: Kubernetes is not automatically stronger

1. **Shared kernel.** Container-based sandboxes share the host kernel
   [32][138]. agent-sandbox delegates stronger isolation to gVisor or Kata
   [33][35]. The OpenShell setup page does not mention either.
2. **Cluster blast radius.** The OpenHands chart warns that cluster-admin RBAC
   lets an agent "delete every resource in the cluster" [45]. The Microsoft
   Kubernetes threat-matrix page on service-account tokens returned 404, so that
   source was not read.
3. **NetworkPolicy may be unenforced.** OpenShell warns that Kubernetes accepts
   policies "even when no CNI enforces them" [27].

  count.
- NVD CVE pages failed to render (JavaScript). The same records were read from
  the MITRE CVE API [70][89][99][100][118][122].
- Only OpenHands has a first-party Kubernetes path in fetched sources [45].

  Kubernetes deployment was found for Goose, Codex or Claude Code.
